Earlier this year Twiggy claimed that Fortescue (FMG) workers didn’t need unions because they cared so much about their employees, who they treated like “family'. Given this you would expect that when the unions representing hundreds of Fortescue workers recently wrote to Fortescue asking to collectively bargain for fair pay and conditions Fortescue would have welcomed the opportunity.
Alas apparently not. 
Two days ago FMG filed an application in the federal court in response the Unions request for FMG to collectively bargain, in what appears to be an attempt to prevent or delay their “family' from collectively bargaining. 
FMGs actions disrespects their workforce, many of whom are union members with a desire to bargain collectively in line with Australian Industrial law. The real questions is, when does the family care and respect for their employees cease? FMGs actions appears to demonstrate that this ceases at very minute their workers start to speak and act collectively.  
The WMWA and ETU always expected Fortescue’s to put up obstacles to prevent giving its workers a real say in their pay and conditions, Members can be sure we won't be walking away or backing down on enforcing our members legal rights to collectively bargain. 
If your a member keep an eye our your emails for our collective bargaining issues survey. 
If you're not already a member join our fight for fair today.

Last week Fortescue advised its workforce of their 2027 FY salary review and allowance increase for most operational and trades employees on FMGs fixed remuneration structure.  
 The salary increase is 4.5% ,which is roughly in line with CPI
 The site and shift allowance has increased by $2500 
These increases are both well deserved and welcomed by members. However, as is the case with many of the Pilbara mining companies, the annual salary increases and increases to allowance are entirely at the company's discretion.
In Fortescue's case, the increases to the site and shift allowance sits in company policy and employees' individual contracts of employment, which Fortescue can effectively change at any time. 
The real question for FMG workers is - would Fortescue have been as generous across the board if the WMWA hadn’t recently sought to start collective bargaining at FMG?
Whilst FMG has sought to delay the collective bargaining process through federal court action, the WMWA is determined to continue to fight for fair at Fortescue.
If you work for FMG and want to have a real say in your pay and conditions join the WMWA today!

Does your workplace have an extended sick leave policy?
ESLs and improved sick leave policies can be life changing, although if they're not enshrined in an Enterprise Bargaining Agreement (EBA) they can be amended or removed at any time.
The Western Mine Workers Alliance - WMWA is currently locked in a battle with Rio Tinto who has decided to cut their extended sick leave policy. Can they do this? Yes they can, but should they? How can this be avoided in the future? By negotiating a Union EBA.
Conditions negotiated in an EBA cannot simply be cut out, there must first be consultation with employees and the union and then ultimately voted on. The best way to keep your wages and conditions safe is to join the union and get yourself an EBA, so join today!

AMWU UPDATE – RIO TINTO DAMPIER SALT
Bargaining officially kicked off this week at Rio Tinto Dampier Salt — and AMWU members are heading in from a position of strength. 
Thanks to the solid backing of our members and the work of the AMWU legal team, the current Agreement remains in place, protecting your wages and conditions while negotiations proceed.
That means we’re bargaining on a level playing field — not from behind.
This matters because it secures your base conditions while we push hard for:
 Higher wages
 Better conditions
 Stronger job security
 Protection of mechanical maintenance roles across the site
The AMWU is fully committed to winning outcomes that reflect the skill, professionalism and hard work our members bring to Dampier Salt every day.
 Strong membership = strong agreements.
Let’s keep building our power and delivering results.
AMWU – Supporting Mechanical Maintenance Workers Across the Pilbara
Give your union a call on 08 9223 0800 for more information.

Rio needs to do the right thing by its workforce. Job Cuts and redundancies are always difficult for workers and their families.
Rio is an externally profitable multinational because of its workforce and they need to start being upfront with its workers instead of allowing rumours and disinformation to spread.
The WMWA will make sure Rio properly consults with its workforce and the Union. 
We will always stand by our members in difficult times. In these circumstances we will be fighting  for members who want to stay with Rio to be able to stay through redeployments, and allowing those who actually want redundancies being allowed to go.
Want to be part of Union that stands up and speaks up for members? join us today!

The Offshore Alliance has zero tolerance for wage theft. 
Whether an employer rips members off tens of thousands of dollars or rips members off a meal allowance, our EBA’s will be enforced by the Union and our legal team.
Which is why the Offshore Alliance is prosecuting Chevron in the Industrial Magistrates Court.
This mob make $billions out of Australian oil and gas and don’t pay tax (or very much tax), yet think they can pick and choose which parts of our EBA they need to comply with.
The OA lawyers are seeking Chevron pay our member the meal allowance he is 
entitled, and a penalty set by the Court.
Chevron are Chevrong.

Chevron have busted their chops to try and prevent the Offshore Alliance being provided documents which show that Chevron have breached our EBA by outsourcing permanent E&I positions to contractors – at significantly lower wages.
 Last week, the Industrial Magistrates Court Ordered Chevron to hand these documents over to the Offshore Alliance lawyers.
 The Offshore Alliance want Chevron convicted of breaching our EBA, Ordered by the Court to employ the required number of E&I Techs and pay a significant penalty for breaching the most important term of all in our oil and gas EBA’s – job security.
Chevron are Chevrong.
